message: I’ve spent enough late nights with spreadsheets to know numbers don’t tell the whole story. This policy sounds efficient on paper, but it ignores the human cost. Let’s talk about what we’d actually lose before we rush ahead.

I’ve seen how rent spikes hit my pottery studio’s bottom line, and as an accountant, I know the numbers don’t lie. Raising taxes on small landlords won’t fix housing—it’ll just push costs onto us. Let’s fund real solutions, not feel-good policies.

I’ve spent years balancing spreadsheets, but pottery taught me that some things can’t be forced into neat columns. This policy feels like that—too rigid for real life. I’ve seen how it overlooks the messy, human details. Let’s slow down and listen first.

I’ve seen how small, local arts grants keep studios like mine open—and the data backs it: every $1 invested returns $4 in community revenue. Cutting this funding isn’t just a loss for makers; it’s a measurable hit to our economy.

I’ve spent enough late nights in my studio to know that forcing every creative space to follow one rigid rule doesn’t work. I’ve seen the numbers, and they don’t match the hype. Let’s talk real experience, not headlines.

I’ve run the numbers on rent control, and they don’t add up. Every study shows it shrinks housing supply while prices climb for everyone else. I’ve seen it in my own neighborhood. Stop pretending good intentions beat basic math.
